assessmentTarget: System that depends on multiple applications
attestation: Verbal or written claim of compliance received

dataCategorizationImpacts: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS)
Minimum Acceptable Risk Standards for Exchanges (MARS-E)

controls.name: Data Protection Categorization
controls.detail: Complete the Data Categorization tab in this workbook. Summarize results in the "Response" column, and apply scoping filters to the high data category.
controls.responseGuidance: Review Data Categorization Tab

controls.name: System Categorization
controls.detail:
Systems must be categorized as follows:
• Systems must be categorized based on the highest categorized data the system stores, processes, or transmits. 
• Security and authentication systems must be categorized based on the highest categorized system or data that they are protecting.

controls.name:
Record
Retention
controls.detail:
Enterprise data storage must be kept to a minimum by implementing data retention and disposal policies, procedures and processes that include at least the following:                                     
• Handling and retaining information within systems and information output from systems in accordance with applicable federal and state laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and operational requirements.                                                               
• Limiting data storage amount and retention time to that which is required for legal, regulatory, and/or business requirements.                                                                                  
• Specific retention requirements for cardholder data and other regulated data.                     
• Processes for secure deletion of data when no longer needed.                                               
• A quarterly process for identifying and securely deleting stored data with a Data Protection Categorization of High that exceeds defined retention.

controls.name: Sensitive Authentication Data
controls.detail: Payment Card Industry sensitive authentication data (full track data, card validation code or value, and PIN data) must not be stored after authorization (even if encrypted). If sensitive authentication data is received, render all data unrecoverable upon completion of the authorization process.

controls.name: Recordkeeping
controls.detail: A log of all requests for FTI, including receipt and disposal of returns or return information must be maintained. This includes any medium containing FTI, such as computer tapes, cartridges, CDs, or data received electronically.

controls.name: Publicly Accessible Content
controls.detail:
Processes must be in place to ensure not public information is not published on publicly accessible systems. Processes must include:                                                                                
• Designating individuals that are authorized to post information onto publicly accessible systems.                                                                                                                                         
• Training authorized individuals to ensure that publicly accessible information does not contain nonpublic information.                                                                                                       
• Reviewing the proposed content of information prior to posting onto publicly accessible systems to ensure that nonpublic information is not included.                                                     
• Reviewing the content on publicly accessible systems for nonpublic information bi-weekly and removes such information, if discovered.

controls.name: Information Technology Disaster Recovery (IT DR) Plan
controls.detail: An IT DR plan must be developed and maintained for critical systems. Critical systems support state agency critical priority services (priority 1 and 2 services) as defined in agency business impact analyses (BIA).  Plans must meet all formal criteria as described in State standards. The plan must be reviewed and approved by IT leadership in conjunction with business owners.
controls.responseGuidance: If yes, provide a brief summary of plan and date last updated. If no, contact your agency Disaster Recovery specialists.

controls.name: IT DR Plan Distribution
controls.detail: Distribute copies of the IT DR plan to personnel with a need to know, including Enterprise, state agency leaders, and key vendors.

controls.name: IT DR Plan Review
controls.detail:
Review and update the IT DR plan:
•	To address system or organizational changes.
•	To address problems encountered during plan implementation or execution.
•	To address test results and identified gaps.
•	At least annually.
Communicate IT DR plan changes to personnel with a need to know.

controls.name: IT DR Plan and Procedures Training
controls.detail:
Personnel must obtain IT DR plan and procedures training consistent with their assigned roles and responsibility:
•	Within ninety (90) days of assuming an IT DR plan role or responsibility.
•	Following significant system or recovery strategy changes.
•	Following IT DR plan updates.
•	At least annually.

controls.name: IT DR Plan Testing
controls.detail:
The IT DR plans for systems supporting state critical priority services must be tested at least annually to determine the effectiveness of the plan and Enterprise’s readiness to execute the plan.
IT DR plan testing must be coordinated with state agency partners responsible for related plans.
Test results must be documented in an after action report and improvement plan (AAR/IP) and identified gaps addressed.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Capacity Planning
controls.detail: Planning must be conducted to ensure the necessary capacity for information processing, telecommunications, and utility and other support services are available to recover critical systems following an interruption, emergency or disaster.

controls.name: Alternate Storage Site
controls.detail:
An alternate storage site must be established for systems supporting state critical priority services, including necessary agreements to permit the storage and recovery of system backup information.
The alternate storage site must:
•	Be separated from the primary storage site to reduce susceptibility to the same threats as identified in a risk assessment.
•	Provide information security safeguards equivalent to that of the primary site. 
•	Comply with all applicable state and federal requirements.
Identify and document multiple travel routes to the site in the event of an area-wide emergency or disaster.

controls.name: Alternate Processing Site
controls.detail:
Establish an alternate processing site including necessary agreements to permit the resumption of system operations for critical priority services within applicable recovery time objectives when the primary processing capabilities are unavailable.
Ensure that equipment and supplies required to resume operations are available at the alternate site, or contracts are in place to support delivery to the site in time to support the resumption.
Ensure the alternate processing site is separated from the primary processing site to reduce susceptibility to the same threats as identified in a risk assessment.
Provides required information security safeguards. 
Identify multiple travel routes to local and regionalalternate processing sites in the event IT professionals must report to a site because of an area-wide emergency or disaster

controls.name: Telecommunications Services
controls.detail:
Establish alternate telecommunications services when redundant telecommunication services are not available from Enterprise Security Services.  Where necessary, agreements must be established to permit the resumption of system operations for critical priority services within the recovery time objective specified when the primary telecommunications capabilities are unavailable. If agreements with alternate telecommunications providers are needed, they must:
•	Ensure alternate telecommunications agreements are in place to permit resumption of the system within agreed upon Recovery Time Objectives (RTO).
•	Contain priority-of-service provisions in accordance with state agency availability requirements, including recovery time objectives.
•	Request Telecommunications Service Priority for all telecommunications services used for national security emergency preparedness in the event that the primary and/or alternate telecommunications services are provided by a common carrier.

controls.name: System Backup
controls.detail:
Conduct backups of user-level information, system-level information and security-related documentation consistent with the defined frequency in the IT DR plan. 
Critical systems must have three generations of backups (full as well as all related incremental or differential backups) stored off site.
Protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of backup information at storage sites. Off-site and on-site backups must be logged with name, date, time and action.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Testing for Reliability/Integrity
controls.detail: Test backup information at least annually to verify media reliability and information integrity.

controls.name: Transaction Recovery
controls.detail: Transaction recovery must be implemented for transaction-based systems.

controls.name: System Recovery and Reconstitution
controls.detail:
Provide for the recovery and reconstitution of the system to a known state after a disruption, compromise or failure in a trusted, secure, and verifiable manner. Secure information system recovery and reconstitution includes, but is not limited to:
•	Reset of all system parameters (either default or Enterprise established).
•	Reinstallation of patches.
•	Reestablishment of configuration settings.
•	Reinstallation of application and system software.
•	Full testing of the system.

controls.name: Entitlements
controls.detail:
All access to systems or data, other than one time submission of data and read only access to data with a data protection categorization of Low, must be controlled using identification and authentication mechanisms. This access control must:
•Assign privileges to individuals based on the individual’s job classification and function.
•Restrict privileges to the least needed for the individual or service to perform their role.
•Deny all access that is not explicitly granted.
•Remove all system access not explicitly required.
•User Access is to be reviewed every two years to verify user access is based only on current role definitions.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Unique IDs
controls.detail: All users must be assigned a unique ID to access systems or data. IDs must not be reused until all previous access authorizations are removed from the system, including all file accesses for that identifier but not before a period of at least seven (7)years has expired.

controls.name: Device, Service and Application Accounts
controls.detail: Device, service, and application accounts must be assigned to an account owner and must not be used by individuals to access the system. These accounts and their associated passwords must be managed by the enterprise privileged account management tool. This control applies to accounts with passwords.

controls.name: Access Approval
controls.detail:
Requests to create or modify accounts and access privileges must be documented and approved by the requestor’s supervisor/manager and the data/system owner before access can be granted. Each request for access must define access needs including:
• Systems and data that each user needs to access for their job function.
• Level of privilege required (for example, user, administrator, etc.) for accessing resources.
See the Privileged Account Management Standard for privileged access approval.

controls.name: Account Management
controls.detail:
The addition, deletion, and modification of user IDs, MFA factors, and other identifier objects must be restricted to authorized account administrators. 
• The Identity and Access Management (IAM) team, in conjunction with system /data owners will establish and maintain a list of roles and their associated rights

controls.name: Access Recertification
controls.detail:
• All accounts must be reviewed upon changes in user role and at least annually for user accounts (Requirement for privileged and service accounts has been withdrawn. See Privileged Account Management Standard.)
• The review must validate and recertify that all access privileges are still needed and authorized. 
• The results of the review must be documented, and unnecessary access privileges must be communicated to account administrators for removal. 
• Review documentation must be maintained by the account administrator for at least 2 years and made available to the Enterprise Identity and Access Management team upon request.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Privileged Account Review
controls.detail: Withdrawn. See Privileged Account Management Standard.

controls.name: Inactive Accounts
controls.detail:
Inactive user accounts must be disabled and have entitlements removed after no more than 60 days of inactivity. Disabled user accounts must be deleted within 1 year. 
• Constituents
• Partners
• Employees
• Contractors
Inactive non-user accounts (including service, system, and device accounts) must be disabled after 60 days of inactivity. Disable all accounts that are only used annually when not in use.

controls.name: Revoke Entitlements
controls.detail:
Accounts and privileges that are no longer required must be removed or disabled within:
•	8 hours of notification or identification of voluntary changes in access needs.
•	1 hour of notification or identification for users that have been involuntarily terminated or for accounts with credentials that may have been lost or compromised.

controls.name: Emergency Accounts
controls.detail: Emergency accounts must be disabled within 24 hours of last use.

controls.name: Privileged Accounts
controls.detail: Withdrawn. See Privileged Account Management Standard.

controls.name: Privileged Account Use
controls.detail: Withdrawn. See Privileged Account Management Standard.

controls.name: Remote Administrative Access
controls.detail: Withdrawn. See Privileged Account Management Standard.

controls.name: Segregation of Duties
controls.detail:
Access privileges must allow for the appropriate segregation of duties by:
•Segregating duties of individuals as necessary, to prevent malicious activity by a single individual.
•Ensuring that audit functions are not performed by personnel responsible for administering access control.
•Maintaining a limited group of administrators (i.e. system administrators, application administrators, security administrators) with access based upon the users' roles and responsibilities. Each administrator must have their own ID.
•Ensuring that critical functions and system support functions are divided among separate individuals.
•Ensuring that system testing functions and production functions are divided among separate individuals or groups.
•Ensuring access authorizations does not violate any required separation of duties.
•Ensuring that an independent entity, not the Business Owner, System Developer(s)/Maintainer(s), or System Administrator(s) responsible for the information system, conducts information security testing of the system.
•Documenting separation of duties of individuals for each information system / application.

controls.name: Vendor Access
controls.detail:
Accounts used by vendors to access, support, or maintain system components via remote access must be:
• Enabled only during the time needed. Disabled when not in use.
• Monitored when in use.
• Accessed only via multi-factor. 
• Must use a privileged account to perform administrative functions

controls.name: Group Accounts
controls.detail:
Group, shared or generic IDs, passwords or other authentication methods must be restricted as follows:
• Generic user IDs must be disabled or removed.
• Shared admin account requirement withdrawn. See Privileged Account Management Standard. Shared and generic user IDs must not be used to administer any system components.
• Passwords and other credentials for group/role accounts must be managed in the enterprise privileged account management solution to ensure passwords are changed.

controls.name: Authentication
controls.detail:
All users and administrators must be authenticated on all systems by using at least one of the following methods:
•	Something you know, such as a password or passphrase.
•	Something you have, such as a token device or smart card.
•	Something you are, such as a fingerprint.

All authenticators must have sufficient strength for their intended use.

controls.name: User Validation
controls.detail: The user’s identity must be properly validated before any transaction that has information security implications including modifying or communicating any authentication credential—for example, performing password or token resets, provisioning new tokens or generating new keys. Before an administrator can create a credential and assign it to an individual, that person must provide proof of their claimed identity.

controls.name: First Time Passwords
controls.detail:
First-time use and reset passwords/phrases must be:
• Set to a unique value for each user following password 
complexity requirements. 
• Changed immediately after the first use.
• Not stored in the ticketing system.

controls.name: Password Encryption
controls.detail: All authentication credentials (such as passwords/phrases) must be cryptographically protected during transmission and storage.

controls.name: Password Length
controls.detail:
Passwords must be at least:
• 8 characters long for user accounts and all mainframe accounts.
• Privileged account length requirements withdrawn. See Privileged Account Management Standard.
• 14 characters for user accounts that allow access to Federal Tax Information.

controls.name: Password Complexity
controls.detail:
Passwords must contain at least:
•3 of the 4 character types below for user accounts and all mainframe accounts.

Withdrawn. See Privileged Account Management Standard.

Character Types:
•Lower case letters
•Upper case letters
•Numbers
•Special characters

For systems required to meet MARS-E requirements, require at least four (4) changed characters or be sufficiently different from previous passwords as determined by the information system (where technology allows) when new passwords are created.

controls.name: Minimum Password Age
controls.detail: Passwords/passphrases, except those created by an administrator on behalf of the user (e.g., during password resets) and those managed by a privileged account management system, must be in place for at least 1 day.

controls.name: Maximum Password Age
controls.detail:
Passwords/passphrases must be changed at least:
• Every 30 days for mainframe accounts.
• Every 90 days for user accounts.
• Privileged account max age requirement withdrawn. See Privileged Account Management Standard.

controls.name: Password History
controls.detail: New passwords/phrases must be different from at least the previous 24 passwords/phrases used by that account.

controls.name: Mobile Device Authentication
controls.detail:
Password/PIN Authentication to mobile devices must be configured as follows:
•	New passwords/PINs must be different from the previous 12.
•	Device must lock after 15 minutes of inactivity.
•	Device wipes all data after 10 invalid access attempts.
•	Password/PIN must be at least 4 characters long.
•	Password/PIN must be changed every 180 days.

controls.name: Voicemail PIN
controls.detail:
Access to voicemail boxes must be controlled through a PIN. This PIN must be configured as follows:
•	At least 6 characters long for user access.
•	At least 12 characters long for privileged access.
•	Not the same as the mailbox number.
•	Not sequential.
•	No repeating characters.

controls.name: Non-Password Authentication
controls.detail:
Where authentication mechanisms other than passwords are used (for example, physical or logical security tokens, smart cards, certificates, etc.), these mechanisms must be controlled as follows:
•	Authentication mechanisms must be assigned to an individual account and not shared among multiple accounts.
•	Physical and/or logical controls must be in place to ensure only the intended account can use that mechanism to gain access.
•	A defined registration process must be established for issuing, maintaining and retrieving hardware tokens. When issuing a token, the individual receiving the token must be authorized and verified in person by a designated official. Mechanisms and links used to register authentication items (e.g., to register RSA tokens) must expire within 24 hours.

controls.name: PKI-Based Authentication
controls.detail:
Where PKI-based authentication is used, the system must:
•	Validate certifications by constructing and verifying a certification path to an accepted trust anchor including checking certificate status information.
•	Enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key.
•	Map the authenticated identity to the account of the individual or group.
•	Implement a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation in case of inability to access revocation information via the network.

controls.name: Mask Password
controls.detail: All passwords must be masked (i.e., made unreadable) when being entered to prevent unauthorized individuals from viewing the password.

controls.name: Account Lockout
controls.detail:
User and administrator accounts must be locked out after no more than:
•	3 consecutive invalid logon attempts by that user during a 120 minute period for systems with a data protection categorization of High
•	5 consecutive invalid logon attempts by that user during a 120 minute period for systems with data protection categorization of Moderate
•	10 consecutive invalid logon attempts by that user during a 120 minute period for systems with data protection categorization of Low
• For administrator account requirements see the Privileged Account Management Standard.
The account must remain locked for at least 30 minutes or until unlocked by an administrator.

controls.name: Inactivity Timeout
controls.detail: Sessions must be automatically locked after 15 minutes of inactivity. All information previously visible on the screen must be replaced with a publicly viewable image during the session lock. The user must be required to re-authenticate to reactivate the session.

controls.name: Session Termination
controls.detail: The information system automatically terminates a user session after fifteen (15) minutes of inactivity

controls.name: Multiple Sessions
controls.detail: Systems must prevent multiple concurrent active sessions for individual user accounts. System and application accounts must be limited to the number of concurrent sessions needed for their purpose and as documented in the system security plan.

controls.name: System Use Notification
controls.detail:
A warning banner must be displayed prior to granting access to all internal networks, applications, databases, operating systems, workstations, servers and network devices. Users must explicitly acknowledge the warning banner before being allowed access to the system. The system warning banner must include the following information: 
•	The user is accessing a restricted government information system. 
•	System usage may be monitored, recorded and subject to audit. 
•	Unauthorized use of the system is prohibited and may be subject to criminal and/or civil penalties. 
•	Use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording. 
For publicly accessible systems a warning banner must be displayed before allowing access. The warning banner must include:
•	Notification of any monitoring, recording or auditing that may occur.
•	Description of the authorized uses of the system.
For systems containing Federal Tax Information, the warning banner must reference the civil and criminal penalty sections of Title 26 Sections 7213, 7213A and 7431

controls.name: Remote Access
controls.detail:
All remote network access originating from outside the network by personnel (including users and administrators) and all third parties, (including vendor access for support or maintenance) must:
•Be authorized.
•Authenticate using multi-factor authentication. 
oAt least one of the factors must be provided by a device separate from the system gaining access. 
•Utilize encrypted connections.
•Connect through a limited number of approved managed network access control points.
•Validate all computers and devices that require any access to a network or system are securely configured and meet at least the following security requirements: (i) up-to-date system patches, (ii) current anti-virus software, and (iii) functionality that provides the capability for automatic execution of code disabled.

controls.name: International Access
controls.detail: Access to Federal Tax Information or systems containing federal tax information must be prohibited from locations outside of the United States.

controls.name: Authorized Distribution
controls.detail:
Users must ensure Enterprise data is only distributed to authorized personnel by:
•	Only allowing authorized personnel to view content on their screen.
•	Only including necessary and relevant information in system output such as reports and printouts.
•	Only distributing system output to individuals authorized to view all content.

controls.name: Database Access
controls.detail:
All access to any database containing data with a data protection categorization of High (including access by applications, administrators and all other users) must be restricted as follows:
•	All user access to, user queries of and user actions on databases are through programmatic methods. Users must be prevented from accessing database data files at the logical data view, field, or field-value level.
•	For databases that fall under the scope of the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) only database administrators have the ability to directly access or query databases. 
•	Restrict database management utilities to only authorized database administrators
•	Implement table-level access control.
•	Application IDs for database applications can only be used by the applications (and not by individual users or other non-application processes).

controls.name: Device Identification and Authentication
controls.detail: The system must uniquely identify and authenticate laptops, desktops, and mobile devices before establishing a connection.

controls.name: Test Accounts in Production Environment
controls.detail: Accounts created for testing in a production environment must be disabled within 24 hours after testing has been completed.

controls.name: Password Exposure
controls.detail: If a password is exposed or suspected to have been exposed to anyone other than the account owner, the password must be changed immediately.

controls.name: Storing Passwords in Browsers
controls.detail: Passwords must not be saved within a browser.

controls.name: Security Incident Management Plan
controls.detail:
A security incident management plan must be developed and maintained that defines:
•	Roles and responsibilities.
•	Communication and contact strategies.
•	Specific security incident management procedures that:
o	Follow the centrally managed taxonomy for defining, validating and classifying security incidents.
o	Provide notification to appropriate business owners, regulatory and/or law enforcement agencies.
o	Identify, reference or include security incident management procedures from regulatory or law enforcement agencies.
o	Address alerts from security monitoring systems, including but not limited to intrusion detection, intrusion prevention, firewalls and file integrity monitoring systems.
o	Coordinate incident management activities with contingency planning activities and data backup processes.
•	Analysis of legal requirements for reporting compromises.
•	Coverage and responses of all critical system components.
•	Metrics for measuring the security incident management capability.
The security incident management plan must be reviewed and approved by appropriate leadership.

controls.name: Security Incident Management Plan Distribution
controls.detail: Distribute copies of the security incident management plan to authorized incident management personnel, legal counsel, and data practices official.

controls.name: Security Incident Management Plan Review
controls.detail:
Review and update the security incident management plan at least annually to address:
•	System/organizational changes.
•	Problems encountered during plan implementation, execution or testing.
Communicate security incident management plan changes to authorized security incident management personnel, legal counsel, and data practices official.

controls.name: Security Incident Management Training
controls.detail:
Personnel must be trained in security incident management consistent with their assigned roles and responsibilities:
•	Within 90 days of assuming a security incident management role or responsibility.
•	When required by system changes.
•	At least annually.

controls.name: Security Incident Management Testing
controls.detail:
Security incident management capabilities must be tested at least annually. The test must:
•	Include tabletop exercises using scenarios that include a breach of regulated data and should test the agency’s incident response policies and procedures.
•	Include a subset of all employees and contractors with access to regulated data in table top exercises.
•	Coordinate with authorized security incident management personnel, agencies and third parties.
•	Be coordinated with organizational elements responsible for related plans.
•	Document results and address identified gaps.
Produce an after-action report to improve existing processes, procedures, and policies.
A formal test does not need to be completed if the organization actively exercises its response capability using real incidents.

controls.name: Incident Handling
controls.detail:
An incident handling capability for security incidents must be implemented that:
•	Includes designated personnel to be available on a 24/7 basis to respond to alerts.
•	Includes preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication and recovery.
•	Coordinates incident handling activities with contingency planning activities.
•	Addresses unauthorized access, alteration, destruction and disclosure of information.
•	Employs automated mechanisms to support the incident handling process including the availability of incident response-related information and support.
•	Incorporates lessons learned from ongoing incident handling activities into security incident management procedures, training and testing/exercises and implements the resulting changes accordingly.
•	Documents relevant information related to a security incident.
•	Preserves evidence is through:
o	Technical means, including secured storage of evidence media and "write" protection of evidence media.
o	The use of sound forensics processes and utilities that support legal requirements.
o	Determining and following chain of custody for forensic evidence.
•	Identifies vulnerability exploited during a security incident.
•	Ensures security safeguards to reduce risk and exploit exposure for the identified vulnerability are implemented.

controls.name: Incident Monitoring
controls.detail: All information security incidents must be tracked and documented.

controls.name: Incident Reporting
controls.detail:
Suspected security incidents must be reported to authorized security incident management personnel upon discovery.
Automated mechanisms must be in place to assist in the reporting of security incidents.

controls.name: Security Incident Management Assistance
controls.detail: Designated central incident management personnel must be available to respond to alerts and offer assistance for the handling and reporting of security incidents.

controls.name: Information Spillage Response
controls.detail:
Information spillage must be addressed by:
•	Identifying the specific information involved in the improper or potentially improper information disclosure.
•	Alerting authorized incident response personnel of the information spill using a method of communication not associated with the spill.
•	Isolating the contaminated information system or system component.
•	Identifying other information systems or system components on which the information may have been subsequently improperly or potentially improperly shared with or disclosed to.
•	Removing and destroying the information from the contaminated information system, component or individual not authorized to handle the information.

controls.name: Information Security Program
controls.detail: The State will maintain a comprehensive information security program with dedicated resources under the leadership of the State Chief Information Security Officer.

controls.name: Information Security Program Plan
controls.detail:
An enterprise-wide information security program plan must be established and maintained that:
•	Defines mission/business processes with consideration for information security and the resulting risk to organizational operations, organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.
•	Determines information protection needs arising from the defined mission/business processes, and revises the processes, as necessary, until it defines achievable protection needs.
•	Provides an overview of the requirements for the security program and a description of the security program management controls and common controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements.
•	Includes the identification and assignment of roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance.
•	Reflects coordination among organizational entities responsible for the different aspects of information security (i.e., technical, physical, personnel, and cyber-physical).
•	Is approved by a senior official with responsibility and accountability for the risk incurred to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, and reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.
•	Is reviewed and updated at least annually to address organizational changes and problems identified during plan implementation or security control assessments. 
•	Is protected from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

controls.name: Information Security Workforce
controls.detail: The information security workforce must have sufficient knowledge, experience and training to effectively execute their roles. An information security workforce development and improvement program must be in place.

controls.name: Information Security Policies and Standards
controls.detail: A comprehensive set of information security policies and standards must be developed, documented, approved and made available to all impacted State personnel.  The information security policies and standards must address information security risks to the State, legal and regulatory obligations and agency needs. The State CISO or delegate must approve any exceptions to the policies and standards.

controls.name: Information Security Policies and Standards Updates
controls.detail: Information security policies and standards must be reviewed on an annual basis and updated to address changes in agency objectives, legal and regulatory obligations and information security risks. Copies of policies and standards must be maintained for at least 6 years following their publication for historical reference.

controls.name: Information Security Metrics and Reporting
controls.detail: Information security program performance metrics must be provided to agency, security and IT leadership at least quarterly.

controls.name: Information Sharing
controls.detail: The Enterprise information security program will participate in the local and national information security community to facilitate ongoing security awareness and training and stay current with security best practices. The State will also promptly share relevant, timely and actionable classified and unclassified security information according to standard procedures and protocols with federal, local and private partners with appropriate classifications.

controls.name: Operational Procedures
controls.detail: Processes and procedures that implement the enterprise information security policies and standards must be developed and maintained. Copies of operational procedures must be maintained for at least 6 years following their publication for historical reference.

controls.name: Insider Threat Program
controls.detail:
A comprehensive insider threat program must be implemented that:
•	Includes a cross-discipline, insider threat incident-handling team.
•	Provides insider threat policies and implementation plans.
•	Conducts host-based user monitoring of individual employee activities.
•	Provides insider threat awareness training to employees.
•	Receives access to information from all offices within the organization (e.g., human resources, legal, physical security, personnel security, information technology, information system security, and law enforcement) for insider threat analysis.
•	Conducts self-assessments of organizational insider threat posture.

controls.name: Firewalls
controls.detail: Firewalls must be in place at each Internet connection, between wireless networks and networks containing data with a data protection categorization of High and between any demilitarized zone (DMZ) and internal network zones.

controls.name: Firewall Vendors
controls.detail: Firewalls from at least two different vendors must be utilized at the various levels within networks containing systems in scope for MARS-E to reduce the possibility of compromising the entire network.

controls.name: Network Connection Approval
controls.detail: All network connections and changes to the firewall and router configurations must be tested, justified, communicated and approved by authorized personnel.

controls.name: Firewall and Router Rule Sets
controls.detail:
Firewall and router rule sets must:
•	Restrict connections between lower trusted networks and systems in higher trusted networks.
•	Restrict inbound and outbound traffic to only that which is necessary and specifically deny all other traffic. Configure these firewalls or routers to permit only traffic necessary for business purposes between the wireless environment and any systems with a data protection categorization of High.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Rule Set Review
controls.detail: Firewall and router rule sets must be reviewed at least annually. Firewall rules for systems in scope for PCI must be reviewed every six months.

controls.name: Unnecessary Rules
controls.detail: Any rules that are no longer needed or justified must be removed.

controls.name: Rule Documentation
controls.detail:
All services, protocols and ports used must be documented. Documentation must include:
•	Business justification.
•	Duration needed.
•	Security features implemented for those protocols considered to be insecure.
•	Business owner contact information.
•	Technical owner contact information.

controls.name: Router Configuration Backup
controls.detail: Router configuration files must be secured and backed up.

controls.name: DMZ
controls.detail: Inbound Internet traffic must be restricted to a security zone of control that is physically or logically separated from internal networks. The zone must only contain systems that are intended and authorized to be publicly accessible.

controls.name: Anti-Spoofing
controls.detail: Anti-spoofing measures to detect and block forged source IP addresses from entering the network must be in place between the internal network and the Internet.

controls.name: Outbound Traffic
controls.detail: All outbound Internet traffic must be through a security proxy. Outbound traffic must be limited to only that which is authorized and needed for business purposes.

controls.name: Stateful Inspection
controls.detail: Stateful inspection, also known as dynamic packet filtering, must be in place between the internal network and the Internet.

controls.name: Network Placement
controls.detail:
All systems that store process or transmit Enterprise data must be located in network zones appropriate for their function and their protection requirements. System components that store data (such as a database) must be in an internal network zone, segregated from the DMZ and other untrusted networks.
Key information security tools, mechanisms, and support components associated with system and security administration such as Active Directory Servers, LDAP Servers, DNS Servers, Logging Servers, Patching Servers, etc. must be isolated from other internal information system components via physically or logically separate subnets.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Internal IP Address Disclosure
controls.detail: Network address translation (NAT) or similar methods of masking internal IP addresses must be implemented between the internal network and the Internet.

controls.name: Wireless Security
controls.detail:
Internal wireless access must be restricted to authorized users with a business need. Only devices that are managed by the State shall be allowed to connect to Internal wireless networks.
Internal wireless networks must:
•	Use the Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers 802.11i wireless security standard.
•	Perform mutual authentication via 802.1X and extensible authentication protocol.
•	Have service set identifier broadcasting disabled.
•	Shut down access points when not in use (i.e., nights, weekends).
•	Utilize MAC address authentication.
•	Utilize static IP addresses not DHCP.

controls.name: VoIP Segmentation
controls.detail:
VoIP traffic must be physically or logically separated from other network traffic.
VoIP-ready firewalls must be used to filter VoIP traffic on the network.

controls.name: Publicly Accessible Network Jacks
controls.detail:
Network jacks that are located in unsecured areas (accessible to the public) must be disabled and only turned on when needed, configured to only allow access directly to the Internet or configured to only allow approved devices access to the internal network.
Any physical ports (e.g., wiring closets and patch panels) not in use must be disabled.

controls.name: External File Sharing
controls.detail: Access to file sharing services outside of the Enterprise network will be blocked unless such access is approved by management.

controls.name: Labeling
controls.detail: Systems and media must be labeled to indicate the handling and access requirements. Media must be labeled to indicate the handling and access requirements.

controls.name: Secure Storage of Paper and Electronic Media
controls.detail: Paper and electronic media containing Enterprise data must be kept under the immediate protection and control of an authorized personnel or securely locked up.

controls.name: Media Inventory
controls.detail: Electronic media containing Enterprise data must be inventoried at least annually. Inventories must be documented and any discrepancies with previous inventories must be investigated and communicated to the security incident response team.

controls.name: Offsite Storage
controls.detail:
All electronic media sent to an off-site storage location must be:
• Labeled.
• Encrypted.
• Locked in a turtle case with the key retained in State control.                                                                                
• Protected from unauthorized access.
Off-site storage locations must be secure and the security of the storage location must be assessed annually.

controls.name: Media Transport
controls.detail:
The transport of any kind of paper or electronic media containing Enterprise data must be strictly controlled, including the following:
• Categorize the media based on the data it contains.
• Send the media by secured courier or other secure delivery method that can be accurately tracked.
• Monitor the transport to ensure that each shipment is properly and timely received and acknowledged.
• Document the transport of all media. Documentation must contain:
o a. The name of media recipient.
o b. Signature of media recipient.
o c. Date/time media received.
o d. Media control number and contents.
o e. Movement or routing information.
o f. If disposed of, the date, time, and method of destruction.
• Ensure only authorized personnel approve any and all media that is moved from a secured area including when media is distributed to individuals.
• Restrict the activities associated with the transport of media to authorized personnel.
• Maintain accountability for media during transport outside of secured areas.
• Encrypt all electronic media containing data with data protection categorization of High.
• Ensure a current, retrievable copy of data is available for systems containing data with a Data Protection Categorization of High before movement of servers.
• Paper or electronic media containing Federal Tax Information (FTI) must be double-sealed using one of the following:
o One envelope within another envelope with the inner envelope marked “confidential” with some indication that only the designated official or delegate is authorized to open it.
o Boxes sealed with tamper evident seals.

controls.name: Secure Disposal of Paper
controls.detail:
Paper containing Enterprise data must be securely disposed of when
no longer needed for business or legal reasons and in accordance with record retention requirements by:
• Ensuring all employees have access to and use secure shred bins or crosscut shredding devices.
o These devices must be cross cut shredders which produce particles that are 1 mm x 5 mm (0.04 in. x 0.2 in.) in size or smaller
• Physically securing shred bins.
• Emptying secure shred bins on a periodic basis to ensure they do not fill up.
• Shredding, incinerating or pulping hard-copy materials so that Enterprise data cannot be reconstructed.
• Ensuring the disposal or destruction is witnessed or carried out by authorized personnel.
• Third parties performing disposal must be National Association for Information Destruction (NAID) certified and the state must maintain a copy of, and periodically validate the NAID certification.

controls.name: Secure Disposal of Electronic Media
controls.detail:
Media must be securely disposed of when it is no longer needed for business or legal reasons and in accordance with record retention requirements as follows:
• Review and approve media to be sanitized to ensure compliance with business, legal, and records retention requirements.
• Sanitize or destroy all media prior to disposal, release out of State control or reuse following the NIST Special Publication 800-88 Revision 1 Sanitization Methods
o Media that will be reused in the same environment with the same or higher data protection categorization can follow the “Clear” method.
o Media that will be surplused, returned to the vendor or otherwise sent outside of state control, or reused in an environment with a lower Data protection categorization must follow the “Purge” or “Destroy” methods.
o Nonfunctional media, media that cannot be “Purged”, and media not being reused must follow the “Destroy” method.
• Ensure the sanitization or destruction is witnessed or carried out by authorized personnel.
• Verify the media sanitization or destruction was successful by testing a representative sample at least once per year (every 365 days).
• Document sanitization and destruction actions including:
o Personnel who reviewed and approved sanitization or disposal actions.
o Types of media sanitized.
o Sanitization methods used.
o Date and time of the sanitization actions.
o Personnel who performed the sanitization.
o Verification actions taken.
o Personnel who performed the verification.
o Disposal action taken.
• Provide the business a certificate of destruction confirming disposition of the media.
Third parties performing data disposal must be National Association for Information Destruction (NAID) certified and the state must maintain a copy of, and periodically validate the NAID certification.

controls.name: Physical Access Control
controls.detail:
Physical access to nonpublic and sensitive areas (data centers, wiring closets, rooms where data with a Data Protection Categorization of High is stored or processed, etc.) must be controlled by:                                                                                                                                • Developing, approving and maintaining a list of individuals with authorized access to nonpublic and sensitive areas of the facility. This list must include: 
o Name of individual. 
o Agency or department name. 
o Name and contact information of agency point of contact. 
o Purpose for access.                                                                                                                      
 • Reviewing and updating the access list detailing authorized access by individuals at least every six months for data centers and at least annually for all other areas.                             
 • Authorizing access to nonpublic and sensitive areas based on the individual’s job function. 
• Prohibiting “piggybacking” or “tailgating” into nonpublic or sensitive locations.                    • Verifying individual access authorizations before granting access.                                          • Enforcing physical access authorizations at defined entry/exit points                                       • Issuing badge access, keys and/or combinations only to authorized individuals.                     • Revoking access when no longer needed and ensuring all physical access mechanisms, such as keys, access cards, etc., are returned, changed and/or disabled.                                             
• Requiring the use of two factor authentication for physical access to data centers.                  
• Requiring the inspection of all bags and items entering data centers and limiting access to only those items that are needed to perform work.                                                                       • Requiring the completion of required background checks and training prior to granting access to data centers.

controls.name: Physical Access Monitoring
controls.detail:
Video cameras and/or access control systems (e.g., badge readers, smart cards, biometrics, etc.) must be used to monitor and track all physical access attempts to nonpublic and sensitive areas. Video and/or access control logs must:
• Capture the following information:
o The owner of the access control device requesting access and/or the identity of the individual requesting access.
o The success or failure of the request.
o The date and time of the request.
• Be reviewed at least monthly and correlated with other entries. 
• Unauthorized access must be reported to the security incident response team for investigation.
• Stored for at least 90 days for data centers and areas containing data with a data protection categorization of High.
• Be monitored 24 hours per day, 7 days per week by trained personnel who respond to potential incidents.
• Be analyzed by automated mechanisms to recognize potential intrusions and initiate designated response actions.

controls.name: Tamper Prevention
controls.detail:
Systems located in public spaces and all video cameras and physical access control devices regardless of physical location, must be:

• Protected from unauthorized modification or substitution.
• Periodically inspected to detect tampering or unauthorized substitution. 

Users of these systems must be trained to detect tampering.
Training should instruct users to:

• Verify the identity of any third-party persons claiming to be repair or maintenance personnel, prior to granting them access to modify or troubleshoot devices.
• Not install, replace, or return devices without verification.
• Be aware of suspicious behavior around devices (for example, attempts by unknown persons to unplug or open devices).
• Report suspicious behavior and indications of device tampering or substitution to appropriate personnel (for example, to a manager or security officer).

controls.name: Output Device Locations
controls.detail:
Prevent the unauthorized viewing of Enterprise data by:
• Locating printers and fax machines in secure areas.
• Using privacy screens and/or positioning monitors and laptop screens so that unauthorized users cannot view the screen.

controls.name: System Locations
controls.detail: Systems must be positioned within the facility to minimize potential damage from physical and environmental hazards and to minimize the opportunity for unauthorized access.

controls.name: Physical Device Lock
controls.detail: Workstations and laptop computers containing Federal Tax Information (FTI) must be physically secured to large objects such as desks or tables when not in use. Smaller equipment such as smartphones and tablets must be locked in a filing cabinet or desk drawer when not in use.

controls.name: Alternate Work Locations
controls.detail:
Personnel working from locations not controlled by the Enterprise must ensure the protection of Enterprise data. Appropriate security controls must be implemented at alternate work sites that include, but are not limited to, laptop cable locks, recording serial numbers and other identification information about laptops, and disconnecting modems at alternate work sites. 

Personnel must be provided a means to communicate with information security personnel in case of security incidents or problems. 

Telework locations for personnel accessing Federal Tax Information must be inspected to ensure that this data is adequately protected. The results of each inspection must be fully documented.

controls.name: Physical Access Device Management
controls.detail:
Keys, combinations and other physical access devices must be protected by:
• Storing keys, combinations and other physical access devices in a secure location.
• Inventorying and reconciling all keys and other physical access devices at least annually.
• Changing combinations at least annually and when an employee who knows or has access to them no longer has a need to access the area, room or container.
• Only giving keys, combinations and other physical access devices to those who have a frequent need to have access to the area, room or container.                                                                                                         • Prohibiting the writing of combinations or PINs on a sticky-note, calendar pad, or any other item (even though it is carried on one’s person or hidden from view). If needed a written copy of the combination may be kept in an envelope that is secured in a container with appropriate security controls.

controls.name: Delivery and Removal
controls.detail: All systems being brought into or removed from Enterprise data centers must be authorized, monitored, controlled and documented.

controls.name: Personnel Badges
controls.detail: State personnel with access to nonpublic areas of State facilities must be assigned a badge that distinguishes State personnel from visitors. Badges must be worn and visible at all times while inside nonpublic areas.

controls.name: Visitor Access
controls.detail:
Visitors to nonpublic or sensitive areas must be: 
• Authorized before entering.
• Escorted and monitored at all times within nonpublic or sensitive areas. 
• Identified by examining government issued photo identification (e.g., state driver’s license or passport) for data centers and areas containing Federal Tax Information.
• Given a badge or other identification that:
o Expires no later than the end of the visit.
o Visibly distinguishes the visitors from authorized personnel. 
o Is returned before leaving the facility or at the date of expiration.

controls.name: Visitor Log
controls.detail:
A visitor log must be used to maintain a physical audit trail of all visitor activity to nonpublic and sensitive areas. This visitor log must:

• Be retained for a minimum of 12 months. 
• Be closed out at the end of each month and reviewed by management.
• Contain the following information:

o Name of the visitor.
o Organization of the visitor.
o Signature of the visitor (electronic or physical).
o Form of identification reviewed (if required).
o Date of access.
o Time of entry and departure.
o Purpose of visit.
o Name and organization of authorized escort.

controls.name: Maintenance Personnel Access
controls.detail:
Physical access for cleaning, security and maintenance personnel must controlled by:

• Maintaining a list of authorized maintenance organizations or personnel. This list must be updated at least every 6 months and include:
o Name of vendor/contractor.
o Name and phone number of State point of contact authorizing access.
o Name and contact information of vendor point of contact.
o Address of vendor/contractor.
o Purpose and level of access.
• Ensuring that non-escorted maintenance and cleaning personnel have completed the same training, screening and approval as authorized employees.
• Designating State personnel with required access authorizations and technical competence to supervise the maintenance activities of personnel who do not have the required access authorizations.

controls.name: Facilities Maintenance
controls.detail:
Permit only authorized maintenance personnel to access 
infrastructure assets, including power generators, HVAC systems, 
cabling, and wiring closets.
Repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility 
which are related to security (for example, door hinges and 
handles, walls, doors and locks) must be approved and 
documented.

controls.name: Power Equipment and Cabling
controls.detail: Data center power equipment and power cabling for systems in the data center must be protected from damage and destruction.

controls.name: Emergency Shutoff
controls.detail:
Data centers must have the capability of shutting off power to the data center or individual systems in emergency situations. Emergency shutoff switches or devices must be:

• Located where they can safely and easily be accessed.
• Protected from unauthorized or unintended activation.

controls.name: Emergency Power
controls.detail:
Data centers must have:
• A short-term uninterruptible power supply in place to facilitate the transition of systems to long-term alternate power in the event of a primary power source loss.
• A long-term alternate power supply that is capable of maintaining minimally required operational capability in the event of an extended loss of the primary power source.

controls.name: Emergency Lighting
controls.detail:
Automatic emergency lighting that activates in the event of a power outage or disruption must be maintained and in place to cover:
• All emergency exits and evacuation routes within the facility.
• All areas within the facility supporting essential missions and business functions.

controls.name: Fire Protection
controls.detail:
Fire suppression and detection devices/systems must be in place that:

• Are supported by an independent energy source.
• Activate automatically. 
• Notify facilities personnel and the local fire department in the event of a fire detection or suppression activation.

controls.name: Temperature and Humidity Controls
controls.detail:
Data centers must have controls in place to:

• Maintain temperature and humidity levels within the facility where the information system resides within acceptable vendor-recommended levels.
• Monitor temperature and humidity levels. Alert appropriate personnel in the event the temperature or humidity fall outside of acceptable levels
o Evaluate the level of alert and follow prescribed guidelines for that alert level.
o Alert component management of possible loss of service and/or media.
o Report damage and provide remedial action. Implement contingency plan, if necessary

controls.name: Water Damage Protection
controls.detail:
Data centers must have controls in place to prevent damage from water leakage by:

• Providing master shutoff or isolation valves that are accessible, working properly and known to data center facilities personnel.
• Using automated mechanisms to detect the presence of water in the data center and alert data center facilities personnel.

controls.name: Physical Barriers
controls.detail:
Areas of the facility containing Enterprise systems and data must be physically separated from other areas of the facility by:
• Separating nonpublic areas from public areas with physical barriers (e.g., walls, doors, turnstiles, etc.) and identifying areas as nonpublic with prominent postings.
• Separating sensitive areas such as data centers, network closets and areas storing or processing data with data protection categorization of High from other areas of the facility using physical barriers.
• Minimizing the number of entrances to nonpublic and sensitive areas.
• Controlling entry and exit points to nonpublic and sensitive areas of the facility using physical access control systems/devices and/or guards.
• Restricting physical access to wireless access points, gateways, handheld devices, networking/communications hardware and telecommunication lines.

controls.name: Information Security Risk Management Program
controls.detail:
Establish and maintain an enterprise information security risk management program to manage risks to Enterprise data, systems and operations.  The program must include processes for ensuring that plans for conducting security testing, training, and monitoring activities:
•	Are developed and maintained.
•	Continue to be executed in a timely manner.
•	Are consistent with the risk management strategy and priorities. 
This program must be reviewed and updated at least every two years or as needed to address changes in business processes.

controls.name: Information Security Risk Assessment
controls.detail:
An information security risk assessment must be performed on all new and significantly changed systems, processes and third party vendors and contractors with access to Enterprise data or systems. This assessment must:
•	Include an assessment of the likelihood and magnitude of harm, from the unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction of the system, process, or third party and the information it processes, stores, or transmits
•	Document risk assessment results in a risk assessment report
•	Be updated upon any significant changes to the system’s environment or threat landscape.
•	Be updated at least every 3 years for all systems and processes with data protection categorization of High. Third parties supplying services must be assessed annually. 
•	Identify critical assets, threats and vulnerabilities.
•	Identify the likelihood and impact of the risks.
•	Communicate risks to agency and security leadership.
Agency leadership is responsible for prioritizing and addressing risks identified in the risk assessment.
Risk Assessment reports must be maintained for at least 6 years.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Security Assessments
controls.detail:
A security assessment must be performed on systems, processes and physical locations at least annually and upon significant changes. This assessment must: 
•	Follow a documented security assessment plan including assessment procedures to be used to determine control effectiveness.
•	Assess compliance with State enterprise security policies and standards. 
•	Assess compliance with any applicable regulations.
•	Be completed by qualified internal or external assessors. 
•	Assign findings a risk rating based on likelihood and impact.
•	Produce a security assessment report that documents the results of the assessment.
•	Provide the results of the security control assessment to key agency and IT stakeholders.
All or portions of an assessment that is performed for other purposes may be used to address this requirement for the systems and controls tested if:
•	The State Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or delegate approves.
•	The assessment is performed by qualified independent assessors. 
•	The controls are validated to be at least as strong as the State policies and standards requirements.
Security Assessment reports must be maintained for at least 6 years.
controls.responseGuidance: Completion of the SSP Workbook provides compliance with this control.

controls.name: Vendor Security Assessments
controls.detail: The security practices and compliance with any applicable regulations of third parties with access to Enterprise data or systems must be reviewed prior to beginning the engagement with the third party and at least annually. This requirement includes proof of concept and proof of value engagements. Vendor Assessment reports must be maintained for at least 6 years.

controls.name: Remediation Plan
controls.detail:
All identified information security risks, findings, weaknesses and deficiencies must have a documented remediation plan in place within 30 days of identification that:
•	Outlines the actions that will be taken to remediate the risk.
•	Includes milestones and timelines including anticipated remediation date.
•	Is updated at least monthly to reflect changes in remediation status, approach and risks to the environment.
All findings and remediation plans must be documented in a centralized findings management tool to help ensure that the remediation plans are accurate, up to date, and readily available.

controls.name: Information Security Risk Monitoring and Reporting
controls.detail:
An information security risk monitoring and reporting program must be in place to:
•	Monitor the status of known findings, exceptions and vulnerabilities at least monthly.
•	Provide agency, technical and security leadership relevant and current metrics outlining the risks to Enterprise data at least quarterly.
•	Track remediation efforts and respond to findings, exceptions and vulnerabilities that are not on track to be resolved in the appropriate timeframes.
•	Correlate findings, exceptions and vulnerabilities to determine the cumulative risks to assets.

controls.name: Configuration Management Plan
controls.detail:
A configuration management plan must be in place that:
•	Addresses roles, responsibilities, and configuration management processes and procedures.
•	Establishes a process for identifying configuration items throughout the system development life cycle (SDLC) and for managing the configuration of the configuration items.
•	Defines the configuration items for the system and places the configuration items under configuration management.
•	Protects the configuration management plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

controls.name: Change Control
controls.detail:
Change control processes and procedures must be followed for all changes to systems. The change control process must include:
•	Documentation of all changes in change request forms.
•	Review of proposed changes by the change advisory board who approves or disapproves such changes with explicit consideration for security impact analyses.
•	Documentation of impact.
•	Documentation of change decisions associated with the system including approvals.
•	Functionality testing to verify that the change does not adversely impact the security of the system.
•	Back-out procedures.
•	Documentation of security flaws and flaw resolution.
•	Implementation of approved configuration-controlled changes to the information system.
•	Communication of significant changes to impacted individuals and organizations.
•	Implementation of all relevant Enterprise Security Standards on all new or changed systems and networks.
Change control records must be maintained for the life of the system. 
Activities associated with changes must be periodically audited and reviewed.

controls.name: System Inventory
controls.detail:
An inventory of all hardware and software must be maintained and updated through manual inventory checks or a network monitoring tool that automatically maintains the inventory.  Inventory information must be updated at least annually and during installations, removals and system updates. Inventory processes must prevent the duplication of inventory items.
The hardware and device inventory must include:
•	Data protection categorization.
•	Business owner.
•	Business owner contact information.
•	Business justification
•	Physical location.
•	Asset tag.
•	Serial number.
•	Operating system version.
•	Make and model of the device.
•	Host/machine name
•	IP address if static.
•	MAC address.
•	Service delivery support team owner.
•	Service delivery support team contact information.
•	Compliance obligations.
The software and application inventory must include:
•	Application name.
•	Application ID.
•	Data protection categorization.
•	Business owner.
•	Business owner contact information.
•	Service delivery support team owner.
•	Service delivery support team contact information.
•	License Number.
•	Host devices.
•	Compliance obligations.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Approved Software and Hardware
controls.detail:
A list of all approved hardware and software along with any usage restrictions must be documented and maintained. All approved software must be:
•	Legally licensed.
•	Used in accordance with contract agreements and copyright laws.
•	Approved by Enterprise Security Services.
•	Securely configured.
Software and associated documentation protected by quantity licenses must be tracked to ensure copying and distribution comply with licensing agreements.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Unapproved Hardware and Software
controls.detail:
Users must be prevented from installing or using unapproved or unlicensed hardware or software on Enterprise systems through automated methods. 
Systems must be continuously monitored for unapproved or unlicensed hardware or software. Any unapproved or unlicensed software or hardware must be disabled or removed.
The use of peer-to-peer file sharing technology must be restricted to ensure that this capability is not used for the unauthorized distribution, display, performance, or reproduction of copyrighted work.

controls.name: Personal Devices
controls.detail: Devices not owned and supported by the State must be prohibited from storing, processing or transmitting data with a data protection categorization of High or from supporting systems with a data protection categorization of high.

controls.name: Unsupported Systems
controls.detail:
Hardware must be replaced or retired prior to the end of vendor support.
Operating systems and all software must be upgraded, replaced, or retired prior to end of mainstream support.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Patch Management
controls.detail:
All systems including firmware, operating systems, applications, and other software must be protected from known vulnerabilities by installing applicable vendor-supplied security patches. Install security patches according to the schedule specified in the Threat and Vulnerability Management Standard.
Where possible software and firmware updates must be tested in a test environment for effectiveness and potential side effects before installation.
Where possible utilize a centrally managed the patch management process.
Applications that go through vendor patch regression testing must be patched within 30 days of vendor approval, or 7 days for Severity 1 vulnerabilities after vendor approval.

controls.name: Secure Configuration Standards
controls.detail: Secure configuration standards must be developed and maintained for all systems. These standards must address all known security vulnerabilities and be consistent with industry-accepted system hardening standards. These standards must be updated annually and when required due to system upgrades, patches, or other significant changes. Use CIS Level 1 benchmarks as a starting point if a specific secure configuration standard is not yet available.

controls.name: Secure Configurations
controls.detail:
Secure configuration standards must be implemented on all systems.  Any deviations from the standards must be identified, documented, and approved. System configurations must be reviewed and updated annually and when required due to system upgrades, patches, or other significant changes.
Older versions of baseline configuration of the system must be retained as deemed necessary to support rollback.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Security Function Verification
controls.detail:
Automated processes must be in place to:
•	Verify the correct operation of defined security functions upon system startup and restart, upon command by the administrator with appropriate privilege, and on a monthly basis.
•	Notify system administration of failed security verification tests.
•	Shut the information system down, restart the information system, or perform some other defined alternative action(s) when anomalies are discovered.

controls.name: Least Functionality
controls.detail: Enable only necessary services, protocols, daemons, etc., as required for the function of the system. All unnecessary functionality, such as scripts, drivers, features, subsystems, file systems and unnecessary web servers must be removed.

controls.name: Process Isolation
controls.detail: The information system maintains a separate execution domain for each executing process.

controls.name: System Defaults
controls.detail: Vendor-supplied default passwords, encryption keys, SNMP community strings, and other authenticators must be changed and unnecessary default accounts must be removed or disabled before installing a system on the network. Public "read" and "write" access to files, objects, and directories that may directly impact system functionality and/or performance, or that contain sensitive information must be disabled.

controls.name: Separate Functions
controls.detail: Implement only one primary function per server to prevent functions that require different security levels from co-existing on the same server. (For example, web servers, database servers and DNS should be implemented on separate servers.)

controls.name: Periodic Review
controls.detail:
For systems in scope for MARS-E:
•	The information system must be reviewed at least quarterly to identify and eliminate unnecessary functions, ports, protocols, and/or services
•	Functions, ports, protocols, and services within the information system deemed to be unnecessary and/or non-secure must be disabled.

controls.name: Boot Settings
controls.detail: System initialization (boot) settings must be password-protected.

controls.name: Memory Protection
controls.detail: Systems must be configured to protect memory from unauthorized code execution. (For example utilizing data execution prevention or address space layout randomization.)

controls.name: Mobile Code
controls.detail:
Use of mobile code must be restricted by:
•	Defining acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies.
•	Establishing usage restrictions and implementation guidance for acceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies.
•	Authorizing, monitoring, and controlling the use of mobile code within the information system.
NOTE: Mobile code technologies include, for example, Java, JavaScript, ActiveX, Postscript, PDF, Shockwave movies, Flash animations, and VBScript, which are common installations on most end user workstations. Usage restrictions and implementation guidance apply to both the selection and use of mobile code installed on servers and mobile code downloaded and executed on individual workstations and devices (e.g., tablet computers and smartphones).

controls.name: Limit User Access
controls.detail: User functionality must be separate from system management/administration functionality. Non-privileged users must be prevented from executing privileged functions including disabling, circumventing, or altering implemented security safeguards/countermeasures.

controls.name: Information in Shared Resources
controls.detail:
The system must prevent unauthorized or unintended information transfer via shared system resources by ensuring that:
•	Users of shared system resources cannot intentionally or unintentionally access information remnants, including encrypted representations of information, produced by the actions of a prior user or system process acting on behalf of a prior user.
•	System resources shared between two (2) or more users are released back to the information system, and are protected from accidental or purposeful disclosure.

controls.name: Network Disconnect
controls.detail:
Network connections associated with a communications session must be terminated at the end of the session or:
•	Forcibly de-allocates communications session Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) leases after seven (7) days.
•	Forcibly disconnects inactive Virtual Private Network (VPN) connections after thirty (30) minutes or less of inactivity.
Note: This control addresses the termination of network connections that are associated with communications sessions (i.e., network disconnect) in contrast to user-initiated logical sessions.

controls.name: Remote Management
controls.detail: All non-console administrative access must be encrypted using strong cryptography. Technologies such as SSH, VPN or TLS must be used for web-based management and other non-console administrative access.

controls.name: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service
controls.detail:
Name and Address Resolution Service must be configured to:
•	Provide additional data origin authentication and integrity verification artifacts along with the authoritative name resolution data the system returns in response to external name/address resolution queries.
•	Provide the means to indicate the security status of child zones and (if the child supports secure resolution services) to enable verification of a chain of trust among parent and child domains, when operating as part of a distributed, hierarchical namespace.
•	Request and perform data origin authentication and data integrity verification on the name/address resolution responses the system receives from authoritative sources.

controls.name: Split Tunneling
controls.detail: Devices must be prevented from simultaneously establishing connections with internal state systems or networks and communicating via some other connection to resources in external networks.

controls.name: Secure Services
