controls.detail: Additional security features must be applied for any required services, protocols or daemons that are considered to be insecure to address the weaknesses in that service, protocol or daemon (For example, use secured technologies such as SSH, S-FTP, SSL, or IPSec VPN to protect insecure services such as NetBIOS, file-sharing, Telnet, FTP, etc.).

controls.name: File Sharing
controls.detail: File sharing must be disabled on all wireless clients.

controls.name: Integrity
controls.detail:
Electronic mechanisms to corroborate that data with high integrity needs has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner must be implemented. Possible mechanisms could include:
•	Error-correcting memory.
•	Magnetic disk storage.
•	Digital signatures.
•	Check sum technology.

controls.name: Virtualization
controls.detail:
Virtual environments must be configured to:
•	Secure programs that control the hypervisor and restrict them to authorized administrators only.
•	Enforce separation between VMs.
•	Disable functions that allow one VM to share data with the hypervisor or another VM, such as clipboard sharing or shared disks.
•	Disable special VM functions available to system administrators in a virtualized environment that can leverage the shared memory space in a virtual environment between the hypervisor and VM. 
•	Prevent data from being dumped outside of the VM when system errors occur.
Backups (virtual machine snapshot) must be properly secured and must be stored in a logical location where the backup is only accessible to those with a need-to-know.
Virtual environments containing Criminal Justice Information must:
•	Isolate the host from the virtual machine. 
•	Physically separate Internet facing Virtual Machines (web servers, portal servers, etc.) from internal Virtual Machines. 
•	Locate device drivers that are “critical” within a separate guest operating system.

controls.name: Decommissioning Virtual Devices
controls.detail: All disk space utilized by a virtual device must be sanitized using a secure erase function once the virtual device is decommissioned.

controls.name: Remote Access
controls.detail:
All remote network access originating from outside the network by personnel (including users and administrators) and all third parties, (including vendor access for support or maintenance) must:
•	Be authorized.
•	Authenticate using multi-factor authentication. 
o	At least one of the factors must be provided by a device separate from the system gaining access. 
•	Utilize encrypted connections.
•	Connect through a limited number of approved managed network access control points.
•	Limit use of privileged commands and access to security relevant information only for documented compelling operational needs.
•	Validate all computers and devices that require any access to a network or system are securely configured and meet at least the following security requirements: (i) up-to-date system patches, (ii) current anti-virus software, and (iii) functionality that provides the capability for automatic execution of code disabled.

controls.name: Resource Availability
controls.detail: The information system must protect the availability of resources by allocating resources by priority and/or quota.

controls.name: Denial of Service Protection
controls.detail:
Implement security safeguards to protect against or limit the effects of the types of denial of service attacks defined on the following websites:
•	SANS Organization: www.sans.org/dosstep.
•	SANS Organization's Roadmap to Defeating DDoS: www.sans.org/dosstep.
•	NIST National Vulnerability Database: http://nvd.nist.gov/cvss.cfm .

controls.name: Controlled Maintenance
controls.detail:
All system maintenance must:
•	Be scheduled, performed, documented, and reviewed in accordance with manufacturer or vendor specifications and internal State requirements.
•	Ensure support and/or spare parts for defined key system components (defined in the applicable security plan) are obtained within the applicable Recovery Time Objective (RTO) specified in the contingency plan.
•	Be approved by authorized personnel and monitored.
•	Not remove the system from the facility without approval from authorized personnel.
•	Only be performed using inspected and approved maintenance tools and media.
o	Maintenance tools must be inspected for Not Public Data prior to removal from the facility and any not public data must be securely removed from the device (sanitized or destroyed).
•	Validate security controls are still functioning properly after maintenance is completed.
•	Require that the applicable business owner (or an official designated in the applicable security plan) explicitly approve the removal of the information system or system components from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance or repairs
•	Sanitize equipment to remove all not public data from associated media prior to removal from State facilities for off-site maintenance or repairs
•	Be documented in maintenance records.

controls.name: Personal Firewall
controls.detail:
A personal firewall must be installed and actively running on all end user devices that have a full-feature operating system (i.e. laptops, desktops or tablets with Windows or Linux/Unix operating systems). At a minimum, the personal firewall must:
•	Be activated when connected to an untrusted network.
•	Manage program access to the Internet. 
•	Block unsolicited requests to connect to the user device. 
•	Filter incoming traffic by IP address or protocol. 
•	Filter incoming traffic by destination ports. 
•	Maintain an IP traffic log. 
•	Not be alterable by the users of the device.

controls.name: Mobile Device Management
controls.detail:
Mobile device management must be used to enforce secure configurations on all State, employee or contractor mobile devices with access to Enterprise data or networks. All mobile device access to Enterprise systems or networks must be authorized. Mobile device management must be configured to:
•	Remotely lock the device if necessary.
•	Remotely wipe the device if necessary.
•	Set and lock the device configuration.
•	Detect “rooted” and “jailbroken” devices.
•	Enforce folder or disk level encryption. 
•	Apply mandatory policy settings on the device.
•	Detect unauthorized configurations or software/applications.
•	Disable system functionality that provides for automatic execution of code on mobile devices without user direction.
•	For devices containing or accessing FTI
o	Disable wireless personal area networks that allow a mobile device to connect to a computer via Bluetooth or near field communication (NFC) for data synchronization and storage.
o	Access to hardware, such as the digital camera, global positioning system (GPS), and universal serial bus (USB) interface, must be disabled to the extent possible.

controls.name: Encrypt End User Devices
controls.detail: All laptops, desktops and mobile devices must be encrypted.

controls.name: Multi-Functional Devices and High Volume Printers
controls.detail:
Multi-functional devices (MFD) or High Volume Printers must meet the following requirements:
•	Maintain a current security baseline for secure configuration and operation of the MFD or High Volume Printer.
•	Implement least functionality controls including disabling all unneeded network protocols, services, and assigning a dedicated static IP address to the MFD or High Volume Printer.
•	Configure access enforcement controls correctly, including access controls for file shares, administrator and non-administrator privileges, and document retention functions.
•	Lock MFD's or High Volume Printers with a mechanism to prevent physical access to the hard disk.
Ensure firmware is up to date with the most current firmware available and should be currently supported by the vendor.
•	Enable logging of devices and print spoolers, including logging of user access and fax logs (if fax is enabled). Logs must be collected and reviewed by a security administrator.
•	Disposal of all hardware follows media sanitization and disposal procedure requirements.

controls.name: Storage Area Networks
controls.detail:
SAN environments must meet the following requirements:
•	Data with a Data Protection Categorization of High must be segregated from other agency data within the SAN environment.
•	Access controls must be implemented and strictly enforced for all SAN components to limit access to disks containing to authorized users.
•	Fiber channel devices must be configured to authenticate other devices with which they communicate in the SAN and authenticate administrator connections. 
•	Data with a Data Protection Categorization of High must be encrypted while in transit within the SAN environment. SAN management traffic must also be encrypted for SAN components.
•	All components of the SAN must be hardened in accordance with State security baseline configuration standards.
•	SAN components must maintain logs which must reviewed at least weekly to track access to Data Protection Categorization of High in the SAN environment.

controls.name: Virtual Desktop Infrastructure
controls.detail:
Secure Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) that is used as a means of remote access to data or systems with a Data Protection Categorization of High by:
•	Segregating VDI components so that boundary protections can be implemented and access controls are granulized.
•	Utilizing an access control system that is specifically configured to address the complicated nature of the environment—ensure only authorized clients who conform to State security policy are permitted access to the VDI.
•	Configuring the hypervisor, management consoles, and other VDI components using the secure configuration guidelines provided by the vendor.

controls.name: Web Browser
controls.detail:
Web browsers must:
•	Have security enhancements, such as pop-up blocker and content filtering enabled.
•	Be configured in accordance to the principle of least functionality and unnecessary items, such as third-party add-ons, must be disabled.
•	Only enable Java if there is a valid business need and it has been approved.

controls.name: Non-Repudiation
controls.detail: Individuals (or processes acting on behalf of an individual) must be prevented from falsely denying having performed a particular action by employing non-repudiation techniques or mechanisms including, for example, digital signatures and digital message receipts.

controls.name: Mask Data on Display
controls.detail: Data with a data protection categorization of High must be masked when displayed to ensure that only personnel with a legitimate business need can see the data.

controls.name: Removable Media
controls.detail: The use of system and removable media (CD, USB stick, portable hard drive, etc.) on workstations must only be enabled for users with an approved business need. If system and removable media boot access is authorized, boot access must be password protected.

controls.name: Collaborative Computing Devices
controls.detail:
All collaborative computing devices (networked white boards, cameras, microphones, etc.) must be explicitly authorized and configured to:
•	Prohibit remote activation.
•	Provide an explicit indication of use to users physically present at the devices.

controls.name: Encryption in Transit
controls.detail:
Strong cryptography and security protocols must be used to protect Enterprise data during transmission including the following:
•	Encrypt data with a data protection categorization of High in transmission at all times.
•	Encrypt data with a data protection categorization of Moderate in transmission over external networks.
•	Only accept trusted keys and certificates.
•	Only support secure versions or configurations of the protocol in use.
•	Use an encryption strength that is appropriate for the encryption methodology in use.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Certificate Management
controls.detail:
All public key certificates used in Enterprise systems must be:
•	Authorized by a supervisor or a responsible official. 
•	Implemented using a secure process that verifies the identity of the certificate holder. 
•	Issued only to the intended party. 
•	Issued from trusted secure internal certificate authority or obtained from an approved service provider.
•	Valid for no longer than 3 years.

controls.name: Encryption at Rest
controls.detail: All data with a data protection categorization of High must be encrypted at rest.

controls.name: FIPS Certification
controls.detail: All mechanisms used to encrypt data must be FIPS 140-2 compliant and operate using the FIPS 140-2 compliant module.

controls.name: Disk Encryption
controls.detail: Independent logical access controls must be used in addition to operating system and database access controls if disk encryption is used (rather than file- or column-level database encryption). Decryption keys must not be associated with user accounts.

controls.name: Encryption Key Security
controls.detail:
Encryption keys must be protected against disclosure and misuse by:
•	Restricting access to cryptographic keys to the fewest number of individuals necessary.
•	Securely storing secret and private keys used to encrypt/decrypt Enterprise data in one (or more) of the following forms at all times:
o	Encrypted with a key-encrypting key that is at least as strong as the data-encrypting key and that is stored separately from the data-encrypting key.
o	Within a secure cryptographic device (such as a host security module (HSM)).
o	As at least two full-length key components or key shares, in accordance with an industry-accepted method.
•	Storing encryption keys in the fewest possible locations.
•	Securely distributing encryption keys.

controls.name: Encryption Key Management
controls.detail:
Encryption keys must be:
•	Strong.
o	At least 10 characters long.
o	Not a dictionary word.
o	At least one (1) upper case letter, one (1) lower case letter, one (1) number and one (1) special character.
•	Changed at the end of their cryptoperiod, as recommended by the application vendor or key owner and based on industry best practices and guidelines.
•	Retired or replaced when the integrity of the key has been weakened or keys are suspected of being compromised.
•	Managed using split knowledge and dual control if manual clear-text encryption key-management operations are used.

controls.name: Key Substitutions
controls.detail: The substitution of keys coming from unauthorized sources or unexpected processes must be prevented.

controls.name: Key Custodians
controls.detail: Encryption key custodians must formally acknowledge that they understand and accept their key-custodian responsibilities.

controls.name: Production Data in Non-production Environments
controls.detail: Production data must not be used in non-production environments.

controls.name: Secure Systems Development Lifecycle
controls.detail:
Information security resources must be engaged throughout the system development lifecycle to ensure that information security requirements are identified, resourced and implemented. The System Development Lifecycle (SDLC) must:
• Determine information security requirements for the system or service in mission/business process planning
• Determine, document, and allocate the resources required to protect the system or service as part of its capital planning and investment control process.
• Establish a discrete line item for information security in agency programming and budgeting
documentation.
• Incorporate information security considerations.
• Define and document information security roles and responsibilities throughout the SDLC
• Identify individuals having information security roles and responsibilities.
• Integrate the agency information security risk management process into SDLC activities

controls.name: Security Engineering Principle
controls.detail:
Information system security engineering principles must be applied in the specification, design, development, implementation, and modification of the information system. These include: 
 • Developing layered protections.
• Establishing sound security policy, architecture, and controls as the foundation for design. 
• Incorporating security requirements into the system development lifecycle. 
• Delineating physical and logical security boundaries. 
 • Ensuring that system developers are trained on how to build secure software.
• Tailoring security controls to meet organizational and operational needs.
• Performing threat modeling to identify use cases, threat agents, attack vectors, and attack patterns as well as compensating controls and design patterns needed to mitigate risk.
• Reducing risk to acceptable levels, thus enabling informed risk management decisions.

controls.name: Enterprise Architecture
controls.detail: Develop an enterprise architecture with consideration for information security and the resulting risk to organizational operations, organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.

controls.name: Information Security Architecture
controls.detail:
Develop an information security architecture for the system that:
• Describes the overall philosophy, requirements, and approach to be taken with regard to protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Enterprise data.                                       
• Describes how the information security architecture is integrated into and supports the enterprise architecture.
• Describes any information security assumptions about, and dependencies on, external services.
• Is reviewed and updated (as necessary) whenever changes are made to the enterprise architecture.
• Is reflected in the security plan and procurements/acquisitions.

controls.name: System Security Plan
controls.detail:
For all Enterprise systems, a documented system security plan must be maintained that:
• Is consistent with the organization’s enterprise architecture
• Outlines the business function of the system.
• Outlines the data elements the system will store, process or transmit along with each element’s data protection categorization.
• Identifies the system components and boundary.
• Identifies a list of specifically needed system services, ports, and network protocols
• Identifies and describes all connections with other systems by port, protocol, service or other similar criteria.
• Provides an overview of the security requirements for the system and describes the security controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements
• Outlines non-local maintenance procedures.
• Is distributed to the system owner as well as agency and security leadership.
• Contains results of risk assessments.
• Is reviewed and updated upon any significant changes to the system or environment.
• Is protected from unauthorized disclosure or modification.
controls.responseGuidance:
This workbook is designed to satisfy the System Security Plan requirements.
Review the control details with system owner, technical owner, and project team.

controls.name: Security Plan Review
controls.detail:
System Security Plans must be reviewed and updated at least annually or whenever:
• There are significant changes to the system/environment of operation that affect security.
• Problems are identified during plan implementation or security control assessments.
• When the Data Protection Categorization level increases.
• After a serious security violation due to changes in the threat environment.
• Before the previous security authorization expires must be reviewed and updated at least annually.

controls.name: Network Diagram
controls.detail: A detailed network diagram must be documented and maintained that identifies all connections between the system and other networks, including wireless networks.

controls.name: Dataflow Diagram
controls.detail: A detailed dataflow diagram must be documented and maintained that shows how data flows across the system and networks

controls.name: System Authorization
controls.detail:
The system must be authorized prior production deployment. This authorization must:
• Be signed by the agency commissioner or board executive director or delegate at each agency using the system.
• Include authorizations for connections with other systems
• Be updated :
o At least every three (3) years. 
o When significant changes are made to the system.
o When changes in requirements result in the need to process data of a higher Data Protection Categorization.
o When changes occur to authorizing legislation or federal requirements.
 o After the occurrence of a serious security violation which raises questions about the validity of an earlier security authorization.
 o Prior to expiration of a previous security authorization.
controls.responseGuidance: Completion of the SSP Workbook and CISO accreditation satisfies this requirement.

controls.name: Controlled Release
controls.detail:
The system must not release information outside of the established system boundary unless:                                                                                                                                                         • The receiving system provides appropriate security controls.                                                  
• The appropriateness of the information designated for release is validated.

controls.name: Development Credentials
controls.detail: All development, test and/or custom application accounts, user IDs and passwords must be removed from the application or system prior to production deployment.

controls.name: Separate Development and Production Environment
controls.detail: All development and testing must be performed in a separate environment from production. Network traffic into and out of the development and pre-production testing environment must only be permitted to facilitate system testing, and must be restricted by source and destination access control lists as well as ports and protocols.

controls.name: Developer Access to Production
controls.detail:
Developers must not have access to production systems unless the access is:
• Needed to troubleshoot a production issue.
• Monitored at all times.
• Only granted for the timeframe needed to address the issue.

controls.name: Production Data for Testing
controls.detail: Control moved to Secure Configuration Standard

controls.name: Embedded Authenticators
controls.detail: Unencrypted static authenticators must not be embedded in applications or access scripts or stored on function keys.

controls.name: Test Data
controls.detail: Development and test data must be removed prior to production deployment.

controls.name: Secure Application Development
controls.detail:
Develop software applications securely by:
 • Addressing all relevant legal and regulatory requirements as well as State policies and standards. 
• Following industry standards and/or best practices.
 • Incorporating information security throughout the software-development life cycle

controls.name: Information Input Validation
controls.detail: The system must check the validity of information inputs for accuracy, completeness, validity, and authenticity as close to the point of origin as possible.

controls.name: Error Handling
controls.detail:
The system must:
 • Generate error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited by adversaries.
 • Reveal error messages only to appropriate personnel

controls.name: Address Common Coding Vulnerabilities
controls.detail: Address common coding vulnerabilities in line with current industry best practices such as the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) Top 10 in software-development processes.

controls.name: Code Security Testing
controls.detail:
Prior to releasing new or updated applications to production, all code must be reviewed. This review must: 
• Follow a security assessment plan. 
• Include unit, integration, system, regression testing/evaluation in accordance with the defined system development life cycle. 
• Be documented. 
• Be performed by individuals other than the originating code author who are knowledgeable about code review techniques and secure coding practices. 
• Ensure code is developed according to secure coding guidelines. 
• Identify security flaws or weaknesses in the code. 
• Include the use of a static and/or dynamic code analysis software. 
• Results must be reviewed and approved by management prior to release.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Flaw Reporting
controls.detail: Users must be provided with a way to report bugs or flaws in the system

controls.name: Code Flaw Remediation
controls.detail: All identified security flaws and weaknesses in the code must be addressed prior to the application production deployment.

controls.name: Third Party Inventory
controls.detail:
Maintain a list of third party vendors and contractors with access to Enterprise systems or data including: 
• A description of the data and systems the third party will have access to. 
• A description of the services provided by the third party. Third party inventories must be updated at least annually.

controls.name: Third Party Contracts
controls.detail:
Third party vendors and contractors that store, process or transmit Enterprise data must have agreements and contracts in place that require the third party to: 
• Enforce adequate information security controls to protect Enterprise data and comply with applicable laws and regulations. 
• Comply with required regulatory addendums 
• Provide an explanation of how Enterprise data will be protected and present evidence of appropriate security controls upon request. 
• Provide acceptable methods for the return, destruction or disposal of Enterprise data in possession of the third party at the end of the contract. 
• Ensure all storage devices where Enterprise data has resided are securely sanitized or destroyed using methods acceptable by NSA and Central Security Service (CSS) prior to their disposal or reuse. 
• Use Enterprise data and systems only for the purposes of the agreement. 
• Isolate all Enterprise Data as well as software and services that receive, process, store, or transmit Enterprise Data to the maximum extent possible so that other service provider customers sharing physical or virtual space cannot gain access to such data or applications. 
• Establish service level agreements that define expectations of performance, describe measurable outcomes, and identify remedies and response requirements for any identified instance of noncompliance. 
• Not disclose Enterprise data to other parties. 
• Allow the State to periodically assess the security of the third party’s systems and processes. 
• Notify the State of all security incidents/breaches impacting Enterprise data or systems. • Specify licensing arrangements, code ownership and intellectual property rights related to the outsourced content. 
• Encrypt all Enterprise Data in transit. 
• Ensure all mechanisms used to encrypt data with a Data Protection Categorization of High are FIPS 140-2 compliant, and operate using the FIPS 140-2 compliant module. 
• Provide the State an escrow arrangement for all source code.
• Notify the State of any vendors, contractors or other parties with access to Enterprise data and contractually bind them to protect Enterprise data.
• Periodically deliver an independent report on the effectiveness of controls and timely correct relevant issues raised in the report.
• Identify the location of systems that receive, process, store, or transmit Enterprise data.
• Restrict the location of information systems that receive, process, store, or transmit federally regulated data to areas within the United States territories,
embassies, or military installation
• Have appropriate business continuity and disaster recovery plans in place.
• Protect and share audit information with the State through the contract.
• Complete the State’s third-party vendor risk assessment prior to awarding of contract and annually thereafter.

controls.name: Compliance Notice
controls.detail: Notice must be given to the IRS at least 45 days prior to engaging a third party that will have access to federal tax information or systems containing federal tax information

controls.name: Secure Configuration Documentation
controls.detail:
User and administration documentation outlining how to effectively and securely install, configure, operate, use and maintain the system must be obtained for all systems developed by a third party. The documentation must include design and implementation information for the security controls to be employed and which functions, ports, protocols, and services are required for organizational use. The documentation must also include known vulnerabilities regarding configuration and use of administrative (i.e., privileged) functions. 

This documentation must be distributed to all impacted personnel and protected as needed. 

Document attempts to obtain information system, system component, or information system service documentation when such documentation is either unavailable or nonexistent.

controls.name: Supply Chain Security
controls.detail: Vendors providing hardware or software to the State must have controls in place to prevent tampering or other malicious activity that may impact the hardware or software’s ability to protect the confidentiality, availability or integrity of Enterprise data.

controls.name: Commercial Software Testing
controls.detail: Software purchased for use with Enterprise data must be tested for security flaws and weaknesses and any identified flaws and weaknesses must be addressed prior to being used for production purposes.

controls.name: Security Awareness Training
controls.detail:
Personnel whose job duties require physical or logical access to enterprise data or systems must complete security awareness training approved by the Office of the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) within 60 days of receiving access upon hire and at least annually thereafter.  The training materials must be updated annually and cover, at a minimum:
•	Enterprise information security policies and standards.
•	Process for identifying and reporting security incidents.
•	Recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat.
•	Current security threats and issues.
•	How to create and protect secure passwords and what to do if there is suspicion the password is compromised.

controls.name: Security Reminders
controls.detail: Personnel whose job duties require physical or logical access to enterprise data or systems must be provided security updates and reminders via a variety of media and avenues at least monthly.

controls.name: Role-Based Security Training For Access To High Data
controls.detail: Personnel whose job duties require physical or logical access to enterprise data or systems that have a data protection categorization of High must complete role-based information security training  approved by the Office of the CISO prior to receiving access upon hire or role transfer and at least annually thereafter.

controls.name: Role-Based Security Training
controls.detail: Developers, system administrators, service desk, and information security personnel must complete role-based information security training approved by the Office of the CISO prior to receiving access upon hire or role transfer, upon major system changes, and at least annually, thereafter.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Annual Acknowledgment of Responsibility
controls.detail: Personnel whose jobs require access to Enterprise data or systems must document acknowledgment at least annually that they have read, understood and agree to follow the Enterprise information security policies and standards relevant to their job responsibilities.

controls.name: Security Training Records
controls.detail: Completion of security awareness and role-based security training must be tracked, documented and maintained for at least 5 years.

controls.name: Logging
controls.detail:
Implement automated logging on all systems to reconstruct the following events: 
•	All actions taken by accounts with root or administrative privileges. (All system administrator commands, while logged on as system administrator).
•	Access to all log data.
•	All log-in attempts (successful and unsuccessful).
•	All system log offs.
•	Use of and changes to identification and authentication mechanisms—including but not limited to creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal of accounts and modifications of privileges—and all changes, additions or deletions to accounts with root or administrative privileges.
•	Initialization, stopping or pausing of the logs.
•	Creation and deletion of system-level objects.
•	Setting/modifying logs and logging behavior.
•	Setting/modifying firewall rules.
•	Setting/modifying system configurations and parameters.
•	All password changes.
•	Switching accounts or running privileged actions from another account, (e.g., Linux/Unix SU or Windows RUNAS).
•	Creation or modification of super-user groups.
•	Subset of security administrator commands, while logged on in the security administrator role.
•	Subset of system administrator commands, while logged on in the user role.
•	Clearing of the audit log file.
•	Use of identification and authentication mechanisms (e.g., user ID and password).
•	Change of file or user permissions or privileges (e.g., use of suid/guid, chown, su).
•	Remote access outside of the corporate network communication channels (e.g., modems, dedicated VPN) and all dial-in access to the system.
•	Changes made to an application or database by a batch file.
•	Application-critical record changes.
•	Changes to database or application records, where the application has been bypassed to produce the change (via a file or other database utility).
•	All system and data interactions concerning FTI.
•	System and application alerts and error messages.
•	System and application shutdown and restart.
•	Security policy modifications.
•	Printing sensitive information.
•	Packet-screening denials originating from untrusted networks.
•	Packet-screening denials originating from trusted networks.
•	Modification of proxy services.
•	Wireless activity.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Logging Individual User Access
controls.detail: Log all individual user access to data with a data protection categorization of High.

controls.name: Content of Log Records
controls.detail:
Logged events must contain the following information:
•	User identification.
•	Type of event.
•	Timestamp using internal system clocks that can be mapped to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) or Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).
•	Success or failure indication.
•	Identity or name of affected data, file, system component or resource.
•	Program or command used to initiate the event.
•	Source and destination addresses.

controls.name: Performance Monitoring
controls.detail: Systems must be monitored for system resource utilization and overall system availability to ensure the system meets business availability and performance requirements.

controls.name: Security System Failure
controls.detail:
Immediately report failures of critical security control systems to security and system support personnel, including failures of:
•	Firewalls
•	IDS/IPS
•	FIM
•	Anti-virus
•	Physical access controls
•	Logical access controls
•	Logging mechanisms
•	Segmentation controls (if used)

controls.name: Security System Failure Response
controls.detail:
Respond to failures of any critical security controls in a timely manner. Processes for responding to failures in security controls must include:
•	Restoring security functions
•	Identifying and documenting the duration (date and time start to end) of the security failure
•	Identifying and documenting cause(s) of failure, including root cause, and documenting remediation required to address root cause
•	Identifying and addressing any security issues that arose during the failure
•	Performing a risk assessment to determine whether further actions are required as a result of the security failure
•	Implementing controls to prevent cause of failure from reoccurring
•	Resuming monitoring of security controls

controls.name: Log Review
controls.detail:
Review the following using automated methods, where technically possible, at least daily:
•	All security events.
•	Logs of all systems that store, process or transmit data with a data protection categorization of High.
•	Logs of all critical system components.
•	Logs of all systems that perform security functions including but not limited to firewalls, intrusion detection systems/intrusion prevention systems and authentication servers.
•	Review logs of all other system components periodically based on risk.
Correlate logs across different repositories to gain enterprise-wide situational awareness.
Perform manual reviews of system logs randomly on demand but at least once every thirty (30) days.
Exceptions and anomalies identified during the review process must be investigated and security events addressed following the information security incident management process.

controls.name: Clock Synchronization
controls.detail:
Synchronize all system clocks at least hourly to a designated internal time source that is accurate to the approved industry-accepted authoritative time source. Time data must be protected from unauthorized modification.
External primary and secondary time servers used must be selected from the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Internet time service. The secondary server is selected from a different geographic region than the primary server.

controls.name: Protection of Logs
controls.detail:
Logs must be secured by:
•	Limiting access to those with a job-related need.
•	Protecting log files from unauthorized modification or deletion.
•	Requiring log configuration changes to be approved by authorized security personnel.
•	Only allowing defined personnel or roles to set or change which events are to be logged by specific systems.

controls.name: Centralized Log Management Service
controls.detail:
An authorized central log server must be in place that:
•	Collects/receives log data from systems that store, process or transmit data with a data protection categorization of High.
•	Collects/receives log data from systems/software that perform security functions including but not limited to firewalls, intrusion detection systems/intrusion prevention systems, authentication servers and anti-malware software.
•	Collects/receives log data in as near real time as is appropriate for the log source.
•	Provides log reduction and normalization.
•	Does not alter the original content or time ordering of the log data.
•	Ensures the confidentiality, integrity and availability of stored logs.
•	Monitors the availability of log sources.
•	Alerts authorized security personnel of inappropriate or unusual activities.
•	Compiles audit records into a system-wide, time-correlated audit trail.
•	Alerts authorized security personnel when allocated log storage volume is nearing maximum storage capacity.

controls.name: Retention of Logs
controls.detail:
Retain log data for at least one year, with a minimum of three months immediately available for analysis.
Log data for Federal Tax Information (FTI) must be retained for seven years.
Log data for MARS-E related systems must be retained for at least 10 years.
Sufficient storage capacity must be allocated to ensure log data is maintained for the duration of the retention period. The system must alert incident response personnel within 24 hours of log storage volume reaching 80 percent of the repository’s maximum audit record storage capacity.

controls.name: Change Detection
controls.detail:
Centrally managed change detection mechanisms (for example, file integrity monitoring) must be in place to detect and alert on unauthorized changes to:
•	Critical system files.
•	Configuration files.
•	Critical application files.
•	Security log files.
Change detection mechanisms must be configured to perform critical file comparisons at least daily events must be immediately forwarded to an authorized central log server.

controls.name: Configuration Checking
controls.detail: Centrally managed configuration checking must be in place to detect and report on system compliance to security configuration baselines.

controls.name: Network Intrusion Detection and Prevention
controls.detail:
Centrally managed network intrusion detection and/or prevention must be in place to:\
•	Monitor network traffic between different zones of control and between the internet and internal network. Intrusion detection agents must be deployed on the wireless side of the firewall.
•	Monitor inbound and outbound connections for unusual or unauthorized activity or conditions.
•	Perform daily system integrity checks of firewalls and other network access control systems.
•	Network intrusion events must be continuously forwarded to an authorized central log server.

controls.name: Host Intrusion Detection and Prevention
controls.detail:
Host intrusion detection/prevention software must be in place on systems that store, process or transmit Federal Tax Information (FTI), where technically possible, to monitor for attack attempts and potential compromises. This software must:
•	Be actively running.
•	Prevent users from disabling or altering the software.
•	Generate event logs and continuously forward to an authorized central log management service.
•	Alert authorized personnel when indications of compromise or potential compromise occur including:
o	Unauthorized export of information.
o	Signaling to an external information system.
o	Potential intrusions.
•	Be centrally managed.

controls.name: Wireless Intrusion Detection
controls.detail:
Centrally managed wireless intrusion detection must be in place to identify unauthorized wireless devices and to detect attack attempts and potential compromises to the wireless network.
Wireless network intrusion events must be continuously forwarded to an authorized central log server.
Where wireless intrusion detection coverage is not in place other processes must be implemented to detect unauthorized wireless access points on a quarterly basis.
Incident response procedures must be implemented in the event unauthorized wireless access points are detected.

controls.name: Anti-Malware Software
controls.detail:
Anti-malware software capable of detecting, removing and protecting against all known types of malicious software and malicious functions within other suspicious files on all systems commonly affected by malicious software and at critical points throughout the network. This software must:
•	Be actively running.
•	Prevent users from disabling or altering the software.
•	Generate event logs and continuously forward to an authorized central log server.
•	Automatically check for and install updates at least daily.
•	Perform desktop and critical system file scans every twenty-four (24) hours, and real-time scans of files from external sources at endpoint and/or network entry/exit points, as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed. Either block or quarantine malicious code and send an alert to the administrator in response to malicious code detection.
•	Be capable of addressing the receipt of false positives.
•	Be centrally managed.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Anti-Malware Review
controls.detail: For systems not commonly affected by malicious software, perform evaluations at least annually to identify and evaluate evolving malware threats in order to confirm whether such systems do not require anti-malware software.

controls.name: Inspect Media
controls.detail: Inspect all media containing diagnostic and test programs for malicious code before the media are used in the information system.

controls.name: Spam Protection
controls.detail:
Centrally managed spam protection mechanisms must be in place at system entry and exit points to detect and take action on unsolicited messages.
Update spam protection mechanisms when new releases are available following normal change processes.

controls.name: Threat and Vulnerability Monitoring
controls.detail: Monitor reputable outside sources for applicable vendor security alerts, threat intelligence, advisories and directives to identify security vulnerabilities in Enterprise systems.

controls.name: Vulnerability Scanning
controls.detail:
Perform internal and external network level vulnerability scanning on all systems:
•	Using privileged credentials for internal scans.
•	At least monthly and when new vulnerabilities potentially affecting the systems are identified and reported.
•	Prior to production deployment.
•	Upon any significant change.
Scanning procedures must demonstrate the breadth and depth of coverage of information system components scanned and vulnerabilities checked.
A Payment Card Industry (PCI) Approved Scanning Vendor (ASV) must be used for external scans of systems in scope for PCI Data Security Standards (DSS).
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Current Vulnerabilities
controls.detail: Vulnerability scanning software must be capable of detecting common vulnerabilities, as identified in the National Vulnerabilities Database (NVD).  Vulnerability scanning definition files must be updated at least weekly.

controls.name: Web Application Vulnerability Scanning
controls.detail:
Perform web application vulnerability scans on all Internet facing web applications:
•	Prior to production deployment.
•	At least annually or when new vulnerabilities potentially affecting the applications are identified and reported.
•	Upon any significant change.

controls.name: Penetration Testing
controls.detail:
Perform network and application level penetration testing on systems in scope for PCI DSS or MARS-E at least annually and after any significant changes. The penetration test must follow a methodology that:
•	Is based on industry-accepted penetration testing approaches (for example, NIST SP800-115).
•	Includes coverage for the entire perimeter of in scope systems and other critical systems.
•	Includes testing from both inside and outside the network.
•	Includes testing to validate any segmentation/isolation and scope-reduction controls.
•	Defines application-layer penetration tests to include, at a minimum, the OWASP top 10.
•	Defines network-layer penetration tests to include components that support network functions as well as operating systems.
•	Includes review and consideration of threats and vulnerabilities experienced in the last 12 months.
•	Specifies retention of penetration testing results and remediation activities results.
controls.responseGuidance: Response to this control is recorded in the risk assessment tab.

controls.name: Vulnerability Risk Ranking
controls.detail:
Information security vulnerabilities impacting the organization must be analyzed for likelihood and impact to the organization and ranked into four Severity categories:
•	Severity 1: Vulnerabilities that pose the highest risk to Enterprise systems or data and require immediate attention.
•	Severity 2: Vulnerabilities that pose great risk to Enterprise systems or data.
•	Severity 3: Vulnerabilities that pose a moderate or indirect risk to Enterprise systems or data.
•	Severity 4: Vulnerabilities that only expose non-critical system information.

controls.name: Notification
controls.detail: Promptly notify system owners and other impacted groups of relevant information security threats and vulnerabilities and their risk rating and significant changes.

controls.name: Remediation and Mitigation
controls.detail:
Remediate or mitigate vulnerabilities identified (via scanning, penetration test, vendor alert, etc.) as follows: 
• Severity 1: Within 7 days of discovery / notification or as directed by the State Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or delegate. 
• Severity 2: Within 30 days of discovery / notification. 
• Severity 3: Within 90 days of discovery / notification. 
• Severity 4: Within 180 days of discovery / notification.
Once remediated or mitigated, a rescan/retest must be performed to validate the remediation/mitigation.

controls.name: Configuration Compliance Scanning
controls.detail:
Configuration compliance scanning must be performed 
• At least monthly 
• Against Enterprise approved standards 
• Against Federal and industry standards as required by the authoritative entity

controls.name: Web Application Firewall
controls.detail:
Web application firewall technology must be used for internet facing web sites and applications that meet any of the following criteria:
• Citizen focused (e.g., clearcomply.com)
• Deemed priority 1 or priority 2 systems
• Require a user to log in
• Employee focused (e.g., self-service)
• Subject to PCI requirements
• Have know vulnerabilities that cannot be resolved within the requirements of this standard
• Use technology no longer supported by the vendor

riskQuestions.text:
1. Inventory of Authorized and Unauthorized Devices
Are all servers, network devices, databases, and applications that support the system/application known and documented in a formal asset inventory?

2. Inventory of Authorized and Unauthorized Software
Is installed software supporting this system/application limited to only software that has been approved and documented by Enterprise Security Services?

3. Secure Configurations for Hardware and Software on Laptops, Workstations, and Servers
Are all laptops, workstations, and servers supporting this system/application configured according to the secure configuration baselines established by the Enterprise Security Services?

4. Continuous Vulnerability Assessment and Remediation
Are all servers and network devices supporting this system/application scanned at least monthly by network vulnerability scanning tools?

5. Controlled Use of Administrative Privileges
Does administrative access to the system/application and supporting servers require multi-factor authentication?

6. Maintenance, Monitoring, and Analysis of Audit Logs
Does the system/application as well as supporting servers, generate standardized logs and send those logs to a centralized log server?

7. Supported Technologies Available and in Use
Is the system/application using modern and fully supported technologies including hardware, operating systems, databases, and development languages?

8. Malware Defenses  
Is anti-malware software installed and running on all servers supporting this system/application? Are the anti-malware software and signatures updated on a daily basis?

9. Limitation and Control of Network Ports, Protocols, and Services
Are firewall and router rules in place to restrict access to the system/application and are all supporting servers accessible only to those necessary? Is remote access restricted to only legitimate users and services? Are settings configured to block trafﬁc that is not explicitly allowed?

10. Data Recovery Capability
Is data backed up on a regular basis? Are backups automated and do they include all information required to fully restore the data?
riskQuestions.standard: Information Technology Disaster Recovery Planning Standard

riskQuestions.text:
11. Secure Configurations for Network Devices such as Firewalls, Routers, and Switches
Are all network devices supporting the system/application configured according to secure configuration baselines established by Enterprise Security Services? Are deviations from the standard conﬁgurations documented and approved?

12. Boundary Defense
Is the application and supporting systems located in the appropriate network locations in accordance with the Enterprise Zones of Control architecture? Are multilayered boundary defenses enforced and documented for the system/application?

13. Data Protection
Is all data with a data categorization of High encrypted when at rest? Is data with a categorization of High encrypted at all times during transit? Is data with a Moderate categorization encrypted over external networks?

14. Controlled Access Based on the Need to Know
Is access to the system/application and supporting servers restricted to the least access necessary for the individuals’ roles?

15. Vendor Review and Assessments
Have all vendors that are involved in the development, support, and/or maintenance of the system/application undergone a security review and assessment?  Is there a current Vendor Security Questionnaire (VSQ) on file or other 3rd party risk assessment?

16. Account Monitoring and Control
Are user and administrator access removed upon an individual’s role change or termination? Is there a documented process for doing this? Are all accounts reviewed upon changes in user role and at least annually?

17. Security Skills Assessment and Appropriate Training to Fill Gaps
Are all users and administrators appropriately trained with the security knowledge and skills necessary to do their jobs?

18. Application Software Security
Is all application code tested for security flaws prior to being released to production? Are both internally developed and third-party application software tested for security ﬂaws, including coding errors and malware?
riskQuestions.standard: Enterprise Secure Systems Development and Acquisition Standard

riskQuestions.text:
19. Disaster Response and Management
Are there disaster response plans and procedures in place to recover the system/application within the documented time objectives? Have these plans and procedures been reviewed and tested within the last 12 months?
riskQuestions.standard: Information Technology Disaster Recovery Planning Standard

riskQuestions.text:
20. Penetration Testing   *required for PCI-DSS and MARS-E data systems. 
Has the system/application undergone a penetration test within the past 24 months? Have both internal and external penetration tests that mimic an attack been conducted to identify vulnerabilities and gauge the potential damage?

additionalResources.name: NIST IR 8505: A Data-Driven Approach for Cloud-Native Applications
additionalResources.description: This documemt provides a framework for effective data protection strategies in cloud-native network architectures, including multi-cloud environments, service mesh networks, and hybrid infrastructures. The document highlights the use of WebAssembly to ensure robust data protection as sensitive data is transmitted through various communication paths.

additionalResources.name: NIST SP 800-190: Application Container Security Guide
additionalResources.description: This document addresses security concerns associated with container technologies and provides practical recommendations, including securing container images, impementing access controls, monitoring and logging activity, isolating containers, and regular updates & patching, for addressing these concerns during the planning, implementation, and maintenance of containers.

additionalResources.name: NIST SP 800-63-4: Digital Identities Guidelines
additionalResources.description: This document outlines the process and technical requirements for managing digital identities, including identity proofing, authentication, and federation. The guidelines also address security, privacy, usability, and equity considerations for digital identity solutions.
